answers.core:
This library (a collection of classes and functions) can be either a native asset or be a built-in. There are some pros and cons in both cases:
- Making it a built-in solution will result in lower space consumption (as compiling a shared library requires about 2 megabytes of glue code) and allows to improve GDScript functionality more 'official' way. But most of the functionality will not be used and will just waste the space (redundant code).
- Making a separate addon feels like a 'nightly' solution, but still a good option anyway. As I mentioned, creating an addon will require an additional glue code, which will take even more space than the library itself.
answers.workaround: This library can be a module (please see section below).
